description: The request socket of one head session. A confined head cannot reach herdr, so it asks its own run supervisor, over one AF_UNIX socket the sandbox gets read-only, to perform a granted verb outside. The supervisor only transports and enforces: Identity decides who holds the role, `grantOf` (src/session-host/head-grants.mjs) is the only reader of the grant table and its answer reaches the supervisor in the digest-protected envelope (`session.verbs`), and the verb itself is the Node payload behind `fgos internal head-request` (internal-route.run-supervisor.v1.json).

framing.frame: as gate-go.v1.json: 4-byte unsigned big-endian length N, then N bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one object)
framing.oversizeOrInvalid: the supervisor answers REPLY refused bad-frame and closes the connection
framing.readDeadlineMs: 5000 for the whole request frame (not per read)

socket.kind: AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM, listening, created by the supervisor before it asks terminal-control to launch the pane
socket.path: envelope.session.requestSocketPath: a socket directly in the run supervisor's socket directory, at most 107 bytes (the same rules, the same bind helper and the same bind-back check as the GO socket)
socket.sandbox: the launch binds this one socket read-only into the head's sandbox (confinement request field requestSocket); the directory around it stays masked. Its path is also in the agent's environment as FGOS_HEAD_REQUEST_SOCKET
socket.absentWhen: the role's grant has no verbs: no socket is created, no path is in the envelope, no variable is set
socket.lifetime: listening from before the pane launch until the gate is gone; the supervisor then unlinks the path. A client that finds the file gone reports request-socket-unavailable
socket.peerCheck: the peer uid must equal the supervisor's own (SO_PEERCRED, getpeereid elsewhere); pids are never compared. A wrong uid is answered REPLY refused peer-uid without reading a frame

fields.id: string, 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'
the request's id, null when no valid id was read
fields.data: object, present when done: the verb's own result

args.name: string, required
args.beside: string, optional: the live key of the session whose tab the new one opens next to

head start.does: startHeadSession (src/session-host/head-start.mjs) in the project of the attempt's envelope (envelope.cwd); a live head of the same role is fronted instead of started
head start.data: the object startHeadSession returns ({already, role, key, ...})

order: role: Identity resolves the role to the live session it names and that session must be this attempt's own (role-not-held otherwise, including when Identity cannot answer: the request fails closed)
verb: must be one of envelope.session.verbs (verb-not-granted)
busy: at most one request runs at a time (busy)
run: `<hostBin> internal head-request --protocol 1 --run-dir <attemptDir>`, request on stdin

run.child: started with exactly the step environment of the envelope, the envelope's cwd, its own process group, and the parent-death signal on Linux; stdout is its one JSON line, stderr goes to supervisor.log
run.onTimeout: the child's process group is killed and the reply is refused verb-timeout (the head's own launch waits up to 45 s for its binding)
run.childLine: {"v":1,"protocol":1,"result":"done","data":{...}} or {"result":"error","code":"<the entry's code>","message":"..."}; an exit with no such line is detail `the route ended with exit N`
run.never: the tick of the supervisor never waits on a request: every connection is served on its own thread, at most 8 at once (a further one is closed unanswered)

refusalCodes.peer-uid: the connection is not from the supervisor's own user
refusalCodes.bad-frame: oversize, not one JSON object, no REQUEST type, an id outside the rule, a verb that is not a string or args that is not an object
refusalCodes.role-not-held: Identity does not give this attempt's session the envelope's role; when Identity could not answer the detail is its refusal code only (its text goes to supervisor.log, never to the client)
refusalCodes.verb-not-granted: the verb is not in envelope.session.verbs
refusalCodes.verb-failed: the route child failed; detail is the entry's own code (for example head-key-used, bad-persona, start-refused) or the exit
refusalCodes.verb-timeout: the verb ran longer than verbTimeoutMs

envelope.refusal: envelope-invalid (the supervisor refuses the attempt before the pane is launched)
rules: session.verbs not empty and session.requestSocketPath absent, or the path present with no verbs
the socket path lies in the very directory of the attempt's GO socket (envelope.terminal.socketPath): the same rule the sandbox bind-back applies on its side
identity.writerId, session.role and hostBin are non-empty strings
at least one process step (not a builtin) exists: the route child starts with the environment of the first one and nothing else

trust: the route reads the attempt's own run directory and its envelope as trusted because the sandbox only ever sees it read-only. The guard is the paths grant: a workspace-paths entry under `.fgos` is refused by name (confinement shape, validateWorkspacePaths), so no grant can make that directory writable
log: one line per request in supervisor.log: `head-request <id> <verb> <done|refused> <code|->`; arguments are never logged and client text is cut to 32 plain characters
client: src/session-host/head-request.mjs: `requestHeadStart` connects to FGOS_HEAD_REQUEST_SOCKET after checking the socket file is owned by its own uid; `startHead` is the one branch (FGOS_CONFINED=1 asks through the socket, refused no-request-socket when the variable is unset, otherwise startHeadSession directly)
